title: backlog.py writes stderr as UTF-8 on Windows
goal: The five test_backlog.py tests named in BG-ovulgaal pass on Windows: backlog.py reconfigures sys.stderr to UTF-8 as well as sys.stdout, so its refusal messages (curly-quoted titles) decode in the tests, and they still pass on macOS and Linux.
notes: Needs a Windows machine to confirm. Cause: backlog.py:1057 reconfigures only sys.stdout; the Refused messages printed to sys.stderr at backlog.py:1076 go out in the ANSI code page, byte 0x93 for a curly quote, and the reader thread of subprocess.run(text=True, encoding="utf-8") raises UnicodeDecodeError, leaving p.stderr None. kbcommon.py:49 has a helper that reconfigures both streams; widen touches to _tools/kbcommon.py only if the fix changes it.
